The bound is sharp for constant functions.

input.verdict: Round 2 (Main bound): fail — The claim $\sup_K |f| \le 1$ is not proved (the section consists of the claim plus "The proof is omitted": no argument, no citation, no appeal to any result in the draft), and more importantly it is false under the Setup hypotheses. Setup assumes only $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ compact and $f \colon K \to \mathbb{R}$ continuous; neither bounds $|f|$. Counterexample: take any nonempty compact $K$ (e.g. $K = \{0\} \subset \mathbb{R}$) and $f \equiv 2$. Then $f$ satisfies every Setup hypothesis, yet $\sup_K |f| = 2 > 1$. The scaling is decisive: for any admissible $f$ and any $c > 0$, $cf$ is also continuous on compact $K$ with $\sup_K |cf| = c \sup_K |f|$, so no nonzero bound can hold uniformly over the class Setup describes. Compactness plus continuity yield only that $\sup_K |f|$ is finite and attained (extreme value theorem), never a numerical bound such as 1. The claim becomes true only if an extra hypothesis is added — e.g. $|f| \le 1$ on $K$, or $\|f\|_\infty \le 1$ — but with that assumption the claim is a tautology and establishes nothing. Hence the section fails both substantively (false as stated) and formally (unproved assertion), and there is no result in the draft it could depend on.
